comparisons.finding: A=7.0, F=6.7, overall=6.8. Clear labeled editor and strong submission button. At 200%, the disclosure pushes submission below the captured viewport; reachability is unverified. Orb and atmospheric background add identity but compete with writing. Components [H,T,S,C,Fb,Ac]: editor [8,7,7,8,6,7]; person control [7,7,7,7,6,6]; submit [8,8,8,8,6,6]; decorative orb [6, null,7,null,null,null].

A=8.3, F=8.0, overall=8.1. Best composition: context, labeled question and submission form a short, coherent sequence at both sizes. The underline makes the editor less obvious than the baseline box, but its label compensates. Source provides expansion, focus styling and a truthful preview announcement; no inference behavior is credited. Components: editor [9,8,8,9,7,8]; context/change [8,8,8,9,6,8]; submit [9,8,8,9,7,8].

A=7.0, F=6.3, overall=6.6. Generous writing space at normal size becomes a visibly clipped question at 200%. No horizontal overflow does not establish that the editor displays its content adequately. Sticky submission is prominent, but the distant person context weakens the sequence. Components: editor [7,5,8,6,7,5]; context/change [6,7,8,7,6,7]; submission dock [8,8,8,8,7,7]. Internal scrolling and keyboard obstruction remain unverified.

reason: A wins each specified task through direct ordering and better enlarged-text layouts, for different reasons: immediate writing/submission, immediate check-in, and immediate category navigation. C offers stronger explicit editing recovery; baseline evidence offers richer category cues. None meets the authorized all-screen/all-component A>=9 and F>=9 threshold. Component vectors use [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]; null denotes an inapplicable component dimension. Screen scores combine normal and 200% observations without averaging away enlargement defects.
limitations: Inspected only the six attached sheets, checks.json and the permitted prototype HTML. No prior ratings, other graders, implementation changes or delegation.

Grades are provisional screenshot and source assessments, not a fresh browser interaction certification. Baseline feedback scores concern visible affordances only; runtime recovery remains unverified.
checks.json establishes no horizontal overflow for 18 alternative captures. It does not establish absence of internal clipping, vertical obstruction, keyboard problems or inaccessible content.

Prototype feedback receives credit only for implemented local announcements, selection, disclosure and editing behavior. Inference, eligibility, persistence, actual readers and sharing receive no functional credit.
The evidence B gate concerns its implemented category-control mismatch, not its intentionally absent real evidence. Other below-viewport content is not assumed unreachable from a screenshot alone.

Empty/loading/error states, representative long content, browser assistive technology and full keyboard traversal are not demonstrated by these materials. Source focus styles and minimum sizes provide partial evidence only.

Reported baseline engine, contrast, reduced-motion and performance checks were not independently inspected and were not transferred to alternatives. Physical iPhone, VoiceOver and native behavior remain separate and uncertified.
No modal is shown. Decorative orb typography and task behavior, and feedback for static text, are genuinely inapplicable.
